interpretation: Sample verified for two fresh-rootfs runs and eight fixed-input calls. Callbacks 3/4/5 copy three bytes, a 76-byte component and an eight-byte self-copy to offsets 1/4/80. The eight-byte tail is zero. Callback 3 reads the low three little-endian bytes of the calloc return address: the STORE32 value equals the pointer low32 and its source writer is the same LOAD64 that reads the calloc return slot. Offset 3 retains allocation address byte 2. A 72-byte append to component offset 4 is observed, without claiming the source of the earlier four bytes or payload. The actual +0x268544 -> +0x258b8c callback consumes precisely the 76-byte component. Its uint16 result matches independent CRC16/XMODEM, including the native polynomial table. Callback 6 writes its high byte to offset 1 and callback 7 its low byte to offset 2. Wrong CRC byte order, original three header bytes, initial 0xffff and polynomial 0x8005 fail on each call. Python derives the seed using the prior verified calloc expression and derives the retained header from the same allocation address, then assembles 88 bytes before encrypting with constructor-derived XTEA inputs. Captured pre-block/key/feedback bytes are equality assertions only; actual encryption uses the reconstructed pre-block and independently constructor-derived key/feedback. All 93 bytes match the native constructor and actual AES input. The full preceding ledger is preserved. Only relations, lengths, code identities and already retained final-field hashes are published. Raw pointers, operands, scalar masks, plaintext, keys, IVs, signatures and operand digests are omitted. Component and seed operand generation, allocator policy, AES key/IV generation, general-input and Android equivalence, complete standalone signer and ordinary Cronet six-header online acceptance remain open.
